text.p: Following are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto has said Pakistan is ready to sign any and all nuclear treaties if India simultaneously signs with us, however, she warned that "any step of nuclear escalation by our neighbour will find a response from us."

- Formal talks between Pakistan and the IMF ended on Thursday with the Fund apparently asking for fundamental structural reforms and government proposing some patchy revenue-generation measuers which were rejected by the IMF.
- After about two decades, the Karachi Stock Exchange will resume trading on Friday and analysts said the investors' optimism suggested that the welcome could be spontaneous in the maiden session.
- Pakistan will soon send its special envoys to Afghanistan's neighbouring countries to consult with them and seek their views on recent developments in that country.
- Nine people belonging to Jatoi tribe were killed in a target shooting near Kulab Jeal, Khairpur in southern province of Sindh.
- The Export Promotion Bureau registered the export contract of about 3,000 bales signalling the resumption of cotton export business this season.
- Bhutto has asked the United Nations General Assembly to endorse the convening of a multilateral dialogue for peace and security in South Asia.
- Pakistan Oilfields Limited is in financial trouble owing to levies imposed in the recent Finance Bill and poor marketing prospects for its chromium sulphate plant.
- While the business community is determined to keep their businesses open on Friday, the nationalised and private banks also appear to support the move by business community.
- The Taleban Islamic militia has asked the U.N. to recognise its six-member interim Shoora as legitimate government.
- Bhutto has instructed the provincial governments to resolve religious tensions.
- The 14-party opposition alliance has called upon President Farooq Leghari to dismiss the government and order fresh elections.
